q: A child can hop and stand on one leg. His age is about:
e: Hopping on one foot is a 4-year skill; a 3-year-old stands on one foot only briefly.

q: Which pair shows the CORRECT stage of normal development?
e: Mature pincer grasp is a 12-month skill. Pulling to stand is 9 months, a cross 4 years, a square 4½ years, skipping 5 years.

q: The correct order in which children copy shapes is:
e: Line (2 yr) → circle (3 yr) → cross (4 yr) → square → triangle (5 yr).

q: A 2-year-old child can do all the following EXCEPT:
e: Riding a tricycle is a 3-year skill.

q: A baby says 'mama, dada', waves bye-bye and pulls to stand. The age is about:
The Moro reflex normally disappears by:
e: Moro disappears by 4–6 months; persistence suggests cerebral palsy.

q: All of the following cause motor developmental delay EXCEPT:
e: Asthma does not delay motor milestones.

q: The first investigation in a 2-year-old who has no words but normal motor and social development is:
e: Isolated speech delay: exclude deafness first.
The social smile appears at 6 weeks; limit age 8 weeks.
